Text: The {{c1::public}} modifier allows access from any package, while the {{c2::private}} modifier restricts access strictly to the declaring class.
When overriding a method, the subclass {{c1::cannot narrow}} the access modifier (e.g., from `protected` to `private`).
An abstract class can contain {{c1::constructors}}, even though it cannot be instantiated directly using `new`.
Extra: These constructors are called via `super()` by subclass constructors.

Text: In Java, monitor locks are {{c1::reentrant}}, meaning a thread that already holds a lock can enter another synchronized block on the same lock without deadlocking itself.
A {{c1::volatile}} variable forces the JVM to read and write directly to {{c2::main memory (RAM)}}, bypassing CPU caches to ensure immediate visibility to other threads.
Static variables and static method metadata are stored in the {{c1::Metaspace}}, which is separate from the Heap where object instances reside.
A {{c1::static block}} runs exactly once when the class is first loaded by the JVM, before any instances are created.
A static nested class {{c1::does not}} require an instance of the outer class to be instantiated, unlike a non-static inner class.
Declaring a reference variable as `final` prevents it from {{c1::being reassigned to another object}}, but it DOES NOT make the referenced object {{c2::immutable}}.
